dialogs.title: စကားပြော — In Mya Mya's living room
dialogs.intro: Ani sits in the living room waiting for her tea. She uses the chance to ask the names of the things around her. Watch the ending of each question: the ones with the question word ဘာ end in လဲ; the ones that only need a "yes" or "no" end in လား.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မြမြ|mya.mya.]၊ [ဒါ|da] [ဘာ|ba] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဒါ|da] [လက်ဖက်ရည်|la.hpèk-yay] [ပါ|ba]။ [မြန်မာ|myaⁿ-ma] [လက်ဖက်ရည်|la.hpèk-yay] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.literal: this — tea — polite. myanmar — tea — polite.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [အရမ်း|a.yaⁿ:] [ချို|hchoh] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [မြန်မာ|myaⁿ-ma] [လက်ဖက်ရည်|la.hpèk-yay] [နို့|noh.] [နဲ့|nè.] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Yes, very sweet. Burmese tea is made with milk.
lines.literal: true-yes, very — sweet — polite-statement. myanmar — tea — milk — with — polite.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.id: And that one? What is it?
lines.literal: that — thing — how about? what — Q?

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဒါ|da] [သနပ်ခါး|tha.nak-hka:] [ပါ|ba]။ [မျက်နှာ|myèk-hna] [မှာ|hma] [လိမ်း|layⁿ:] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: That's thanaka. You put it on your face.
lines.literal: this — thanaka — polite. face — on — smear — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဆေး|hsay:] [မဟုတ်ဘူး|ma.hohk-boo:]။ [နေ|nay] [ကာကွယ်|ka-kwè] [တာ|da] [ပါ|ba]။ [အေး|ay:] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: It's not medicine. It protects you from the sun. It feels cool.
lines.literal: medicine — isn't. sun — protect — thing — polite. cool — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဒီ|dee] [စာအုပ်|sa-ohk] [က|ga.] [ဘယ်သူ့|bè-thoo.] [ဟာ|ha] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [ဟာ|ha] [ပါ|ba]။ [မြန်မာ|myaⁿ-ma] [စာအုပ်|sa-ohk] [ပါ|ba]။ [ဖတ်|hpak] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [လား|la:]။
lines.id: It's mine. A Burmese book. Do you want to read it?
lines.literal: I(f) — thing — polite. myanmar — book — polite. read — want — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဖတ်|hpak] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]၊ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [မဖတ်တတ်သေးဘူး|ma.hpak-tak-thay:-boo:]။
lines.id: I'd like to, but I can't read yet.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ရပါတယ်|ya.-ba-dè]။ [မနက်ဖြန်|ma.nèk-hpyaⁿ] [စ|sa.] [သင်|thiⁿ] [ရအောင်|ya.-owⁿ]။
lines.id: No problem. Let's start learning tomorrow.

grammars.title: ⚠️ လား or လဲ — two question endings you must not mix up
body: English changes the word order and the intonation for "Are you eating?" and "What are you eating?", but Burmese uses **two different endings**, and the rule fits in one sentence: if the sentence has a question word, use လဲ; if it doesn't, use လား.

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
The ending
rows: ဒါ လက်ဖက်ရည်လား
ဖတ်ချင်လား
has ဘယ်မှာ → **လဲ**

after: How to remember it: **လဲ asks for information, လား asks for agreement.** If the other person has to answer with a sentence, use လဲ. If a nod is enough, use လား. Choosing wrong won't make you unintelligible, but you'll instantly sound foreign.

grammars.title: ဒါ, ဒီ, ဟို — pointing at things
body: Burmese separates pointing words that **stand alone** from pointing words that **attach to a noun**. English uses "this" for both ("this is tea", "this book"), so this part needs attention.

head: Burmese
Say it
How it's used
Example
rows: ဒါ ဘာလဲ — what is this?
ဒီစာအုပ် — this book
ဟိုကား — that car

after: ⚠️ ဒါ never attaches to a noun. "This book" is ဒီစာအုပ်, not ဒါစာအုပ်. That mistake sounds like saying "this this book".

grammars.title: "A is B" sentences use no verb
body: To say "this is tea", Burmese simply puts the two nouns side by side and closes with ပါ. There's no word for "is".

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ဒါ လက်ဖက်ရည်ပါ
ဒါ ကျွန်မဟာပါ
ဒါ ဆေး မဟုတ်ဘူး

after: Only when you **deny** something does a verb appear: ဟုတ် ("be true"), negated as မဟုတ်ဘူး. So the pattern isn't symmetrical — the positive sentence has no verb, the negative one does. Learn them as two separate patterns and you won't get confused.

grammars.title: Possession: ဟာ and the creaky tone
body: There are two ways to show ownership. The first uses the word ဟာ ("thing"); the second simply switches the last syllable of the pronoun to the **creaky tone** — marked with the dot ့ under the letter.
after: For names and nouns, use ရဲ့ (*yè.*): မြမြရဲ့ စာအုပ် = Mya Mya's book. ⚠️ ကျွန်မ doesn't change because its tone is already creaky — the one small advantage women speakers get in this chapter.

blocks.title: သနပ်ခါး — the signature of a Burmese face
items: The yellow paste on people's cheeks in Myanmar is called **သနပ်ခါး** (*tha.nak-hka:*), made by grinding tree bark on a stone with a little water. It's sunscreen, cooling powder, and decoration all in one.
Asking about it is one of the fastest ways to start a conversation with someone from Myanmar, because almost no foreigners know its name. Try: ဒါ သနပ်ခါးလား။
